mechanism: Convert XAUEUR closes by same-day EURUSD to USD, form |XAUUSD − XAUEUR·EURUSD| spread series, compute rolling mean (or median for outlier resistance), and fire when current spread ≥ mean·(1+PercentTrigger/100); sell the higher FX-adjusted gold quote and buy the lower until spread ≤ mean. Direction of legs can also use short EMA or slope instead of raw price.
data_needed: Aligned D1 (or chart TF) closes for BasePair, CorrPair, ConvPair; rolling window CountQuotes (~250 for annual D1); PercentTrigger; optional EMA/slope buffers.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: XAUUSD, XAUEUR, EURUSD (conversion); also scanned XAUAUD/XAUCHF/XAUGBP; analysis on D1 ~250 days; EA multi-symbol OnTimer.
why_new_for_mis: Cross-quote fair-parity residual after FX conversion is a concrete relative-value change sensor for MIS—detects temporary gold pricing dislocations across quote currencies, not just single-symbol mean reversion.
quote: If we oversimplify and assume that the difference (spread) between both quotations after the conversion by the current exchange rate should be near zero, we may consider any spread above the mean as a tradable anomaly in the market.

mechanism: HiSSD Planner encodes multimodal bars into common skills (cross-situation patterns such as trend recognition/risk assessment) then forecasts multi-step future states from those skills only; Controller encodes task-specific skills from local observations, concatenates transposed univariate observations + task skills + Planner common skills (batch-normalized), and decodes parallel agent actions; Manager cross-attends account state to action proposals. Dual skill layer is intended to stay usable across regime shifts without full retraining.
data_needed: HistoryBars×BarDescr multimodal M1 state; NSkills common/task tensors; account vector + timestamp harmonics; offline replay buffer of trajectories.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M1; train full year 2024 (default indicators); OOS test Jan–Mar 2025 (860 trades).
why_new_for_mis: Explicit common-skill latent as a regime-stable market embedding plus task-skill residual gives MIS a two-timescale sensing split: what is generally true vs what is situation-specific under sudden regime change.
quote: Common skills represent behavioral patterns applicable across a wide range of situations — for example, trend recognition or risk assessment. Task-specific skills, in turn, govern behavior in unique or highly specialized conditions. This dual-layer structure allows HiSSD agents to remain stable and effective regardless of changing market regimes.

mechanism: From Encoder forecast of future bars, take cumulative sum of the close-change column; find argmax of absolute cumulative path over the planning horizon; set a SoftMax/sigmoid direction head target to that priority trend (up if trend[argmax]>0 else down). Gradients from this head are pushed back into the common-skill latent so skills must encode directional priority.
data_needed: NForecast×BarDescr future-state targets from replay; Probability MLP on latent.windows[0]×windows[1] common skills; NActions/3 directional outputs.
why_new_for_mis: Turns multi-step path forecasts into a single priority-trend change sensor on the shared skill latent—MIS can read P(priority up/down) without a separate trend engine.
quote: We compute the cumulative price movement and identify the maximum movement over the planning horizon. The direction of this maximum deviation becomes the priority trend used for training the predictive model.

mechanism: Build main features as rolling std (or SMA) over many periods and meta-features as short-horizon rolling std (e.g. 5 bars); K-Means (n_clusters≈10) on meta-features labels market modes; for each sufficiently populated cluster, train a CatBoost binary classifier for one-direction trade success and a meta CatBoost that distinguishes that cluster vs all others; live trade only when main model and meta_label (cluster membership) both fire.
data_needed: Close series; periods list (e.g. 5..275 step 30); periods_meta (e.g. [5]); train/forward date splits; markup≈spread; ONNX export of both models.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: XAUUSD H1; train 2020–2024; forward from 2024; unidirectional buy (gold uptrend).
why_new_for_mis: Volatility-feature clustering as an explicit market-mode sensor, with a second classifier as a live mode gate, is a lightweight regime stack MIS can reuse without deep RL.
quote: K-Means is used to determine market modes at the preprocessing phase.... A large number of features are not required to identify market modes. This is usually one indicator, such as the standard deviation for the last 5 bars.

mechanism: Extend Actor–Critic with a Director binary classifier of high- vs low-quality actions; in this MQL5 adaptation Director and Critic cross-attend Actor actions to the Planner/Encoder common-skill matrix (post-LSTM latent), not raw market features—classifying actions in compressed skill space. Director influence decays as Critic improves; dual Critics each have two alternating target nets whose average forms Q targets, Actor uses min Q.
data_needed: HiSSD-style multimodal state + account; NActions action tensor; labeled ah/al action sets or near-perfect vs random negatives; twin Critics + target copies.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Financial Deep-RL setting; architecture tied to prior HiSSD EURUSD work (tested in final part).
why_new_for_mis: Action-quality sensing in latent skill space gives MIS an early filter for unproductive policy proposals under high cost/volatility before value estimates are reliable.
quote: the Director operates on a common skill matrix — an informative latent representation produced by the skill generation module at the output of the LSTM block.... As a result, the Director operates in a compressed and more stable feature space

mechanism: Two-stage training: offline uses limited look-ahead to build near-perfect action tensors as positive Director examples and random action vectors as negatives (randomized mix); Critic is trained toward rewards of near-perfect actions. Online (bar-close) uses twin Critics with averaged dual targets, stochastic Actor update timing, and Director labels from realized equity delta (>0 positive); insufficient-funds errors immediately backprop negative Director signal.
data_needed: Replay buffer EURUSD M1 2024; Study.mq5 offline + StudyOnline.mq5; RSI/CCI/ATR/MACD state features; target soft-update tau.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M1; offline 2024; online fine-tune in tester; OOS Jan–Mar 2025 (684 trades).
why_new_for_mis: Operational dual continuous+binary feedback loop (Critic value + Director fit/unfit) is a trainable sensing pattern MIS can use to score candidate actions under regime uncertainty.
quote: the Critic learns to evaluate them in terms of expected reward, and the Director explicitly identifies actions that should be avoided altogether. This creates a dual-feedback system — continuous and binary

mechanism: Compute price ratio series Symbol1/Symbol2 over CurrentZScorePeriod, convert to Z-score vs rolling mean/std; maintain CorrelationPeriod history of rolling correlation; open the pair trade only when |Z|≥CurrentEntryThreshold and current correlation is within 0.01 of the minimum in that history (dislocation + weak co-movement). Auto-grid search periodically retunes period and entry/exit thresholds; optional averaging opens reverse legs when correlation drops further by CorrelationDropThreshold.
data_needed: Paired closes; Z-score window 50–200; entry threshold 1.5–3.0; exit 0–1.0; correlation history buffer; OptimizationPeriod ticks.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD/AUDUSD and AUDUSD/NZDUSD highlighted; also general FX pairs; H1/M15/H4/D1 guidance; multi-year tests.
why_new_for_mis: Gates classic spread Z-score with a correlation-trough detector—MIS gets a joint relative-value + co-movement-breakdown change sensor, not Z alone.
quote: If the current correlation is close to the minimum and the Z-score exceeds the threshold.... moments when the correlation between instruments reaches local minimums, which is an additional signal for entering the market.

mechanism: Replace classical Abbe (Allan var / ordinary var) with robust form: MAD of prices about median as scale, and median of successive |Δprice| as Allan-like speed; optionally use modified ratios of summed abs successive diffs vs summed abs deviations from median. Compare current scales to historical CDFs of those deviations; combine with Kendall direction (distance from 50). Large MAD CDF + large successive-dev CDF + Kendall away from 50 ⇒ trend regime.
data_needed: Price window ≥3; sorted prices for median/MAD; successive abs diffs; running histograms→CDF; Kendall series from prior article.
why_new_for_mis: Robust Abbe-style comparison of level dispersion vs bar-to-bar speed, scored by empirical CDFs, is a distribution-free trend-regime sensor tolerant of spikes—useful MIS trend/flat discriminator.
quote: The presence of a trend can be judged by three signs: a large value of the standard deviation (blue), a large value of the price rate (red), a substantial deviation of the Kendall criterion from the 50 level (green).

mechanism: Trend linearity score = |P_end − P_start| / Σ|P_i − P_{i−1}| over the window; values near 1 ⇒ coherent directional path, low values ⇒ flat/chaotic path (caveat: sharp single reversals can also suppress the ratio). Used with Kendall turns as a filter on whether a trend ending is orderly vs noisy.
data_needed: Windowed closes; sum of absolute successive moves; net endpoint distance.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 2024; Abbe 3 / EA Abbe 3 with LvlMax/LvlMin.
why_new_for_mis: Simple path-efficiency ratio is an interpretable trend-vs-chop regime feature MIS can compute on any TF without parametric variance assumptions.
quote: The numerator calculates the distance between the initial and final values of the time series. And the denominator contains the total distance. The closer this indicator is to 1, the more noticeable the trend. Low values indicate a flat or chaotic price movement.

mechanism: Conversion-Gated LSTM redesigns gate activations: input gate uses σ then tanh composition to stay sensitive to small/large shocks without early sigmoid saturation; forget gate uses 1−tanh(1−1/σ(z)²) whose derivative range (~0–2.89) disperses memory and aggressively drops stale content—aimed at short-term vol spikes and regime-relevant bursts while retaining long context. OpenCL CSLSTM kernels apply these after a shared pre-activation projection of concat(input, hidden).
data_needed: Concatenated input+hidden projections (4 entities×hidden×variables); memory/output buffers; per-univariate weight matrices via conv projection.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Multivariate financial TS; trading stack EURUSD M1 in final part.
why_new_for_mis: Gate-level volatility spike sensor inside a recurrent cell—MIS can embed short-shock responsiveness without a separate event detector.
quote: a sudden increase in trading volume or a spike in volatility may indicate a regime shift in the market, and the timely detection of such patterns provides a significant forecasting advantage.

mechanism: Encoder: BatchNormWithNoise → shared-parameter linear attention across features within each bar (universal feature importance) → transpose → per-channel linear attention over HistoryBars (modality-specific temporal weights) → per-univariate CG-LSTM emitting NSkills global skills → light conv decoder for forecast targets. Task branch clones this stack for local skills, then 2-layer cross-attention of local Queries to global skills before action conv heads; ADC Actor/Director/Critic sit on top.
data_needed: HistoryBars×BarDescr; shared vs per-variable attention params; CG-LSTM count=NSkills, window=HistoryBars, layers=BarDescr; offline+online training EAs.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M1; train 2024; OOS Jan–Mar 2025 (37 trades, PF 1.67).
why_new_for_mis: Ordered feature-attention then temporal-attention before skill extraction is a clear dual-stage multivariate sensor MIS can use to weight which channels and which lags matter under current vol.
quote: At the first level, the model focuses on features.... At the second level, attention shifts to temporal intervals. The model evaluates which segments of historical data are most informative for forecasting

mechanism: VWAP executor loads multi-day historical intraday volume profile, allocates child-order sizes proportional to expected volume per interval (optional adaptive real-time volume adjust), and spaces slices over [start,end]; PerformanceAnalyzer records implementation shortfall, estimated market impact, and slippage vs decision price. Iceberg variant reveals only tip size (optionally randomized) to limit displayed liquidity demand.
data_needed: Symbol volume history (historyDays); interval count; total volume; optional adaptiveMode; decision benchmark price for analyzer.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic MT5 symbol; integrated MA-crossover EA examples; backtest narrative ~2 months.
why_new_for_mis: Historical volume-profile weighting plus post-trade impact/shortfall metrics give MIS an execution-liquidity sensor for when and how large to transact, complementary to price-regime sensors.
quote: Allocates order size in proportion to historical volume patterns.... Executes more during high-volume periods to reduce impact.

mechanism: Maintain 8×8 fair-rate matrix over EUR,USD,GBP,JPY,CHF,CAD,AUD,NZD; seed with direct quotes (diagonal=1); run 3 iterative passes filling i←k←j triangles and blending Set(i,j)=0.7·current+0.3·triangle (and inverse); discrepancy%=(market_median/fair−1)·100; trade when |discrepancy|≥MinDiscrepancy (suggested 0.05–0.1%, higher for JPY). Live imbalance matrix panel is the multi-pair deviation radar.
data_needed: Live quotes for all major crosses among the 8 currencies; g_currency_matrix; timer ~5s; MaxRisk lot sizing; TotalProfitTarget kill-switch.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Major FX web among eight currencies; real-time timer EA (ArbyCross.mq5).
why_new_for_mis: Operational multi-currency fair-value residual field (with explicit iterative blend and risk caps) is a cross-sectional relative-value sensor for MIS beyond single-pair Z-scores.
quote: the system calculates the percentage deviation of the current market price from the fair value for each currency pair.... This visualization acts as a high-precision radar, instantly identifying arbitrage opportunities

mechanism: ACEEMD: add/subtract adaptive Gaussian noise to series, EMD each branch, average first IMFs, subtract IMF1 from original to get r1(t)=x(t)−IMF1(t)—removing high-frequency HFT-like oscillations while aiming to keep turning points; preceded by convolutional smoothing filters f,g and followed by time-aware / probabilistic attention forecasting.
data_needed: Price/volume multivariate series S; noise realizations n_i; EMD IMF extraction; zero-pad horizon p for forecast targets.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Stock/HFT-oriented financial series in source paper; MQL5 article implements probabilistic attention OpenCL path (full ACEEMD wiring deferred).
why_new_for_mis: Adaptive EMD-based IMF1 removal is an explicit microstructure-noise filter sensor for MIS before regime/sequence models, targeting HFT-induced volatility clutter.
quote: By removing the first Intrinsic Mode Function (IMF), which contains most of the high-frequency oscillations, ACEEMD effectively suppresses market noise while preserving the critical turning points that characterize the underlying trend.

mechanism: ProbAttention: for each Query, score importance as max−mean dot product vs a random Key subset (ProbAttentionQueryImp); TopKImportanceToIndex keeps top_k Queries without full sort; QIndexAttention runs SoftMax attention only for those Queries against all Keys/Values (multi-head, shared KV heads allowed). Backprop through attention only (selection stage excluded) for GPU efficiency.
data_needed: Query and float2 Key–Value buffers; sampled index_keys; top_k; OpenCL kernels ProbAttentionQueryImp, TopKImportanceToIndex, QIndexAttention(+Gradients).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Long financial sequences / HFT context in ACEFormer design; MQL5 OpenCL kernels delivered; main-app integration left to next article.
why_new_for_mis: Top-k informative-timestep selection before full attention is a scalable sequence sensor for MIS on long noisy windows—focus compute on eventful bars.
quote: Rather than computing attention over the entire sequence, the mechanism focuses exclusively on the most informative time steps.... attention is evaluated not over the full sequence but over a compact subset that is highly likely to contain the most informative temporal events.
